notable_absence.finding: 21 of the 26 rows in this table (ar, cjk, ckb, da, de, en, es, fa, fi, fr, he, hi, hr, hu, it, nl, no, pt, ro, ru, sv, tr) are stated in an identical template - 'The X analyzer uses character filters, tokenizers, and token filters designed for [language] language searches' - naming a language ISO code with no further distinguishing mechanism given on this page. Per the dispatch brief's own allowance for thin reference content, I did not mint a concept per language analyzer; the registry has no 'language variant of' predicate that would let 21 near-identical rows be modeled as one relation with 21 objects rather than 21 near-duplicate concepts anyway, so this is recorded as an absence rather than either extreme (a 21-concept mint or a false single generalization).

cross_component_finding: TWO FINDINGS. (1) This page's opening line - 'Analyzers contain: Character filters ... Tokenizers ... Token filters' - is the most explicit, least-inferred composition statement in the whole batch, more direct than create-custom-analyzer.json's procedural evidence. I attached it to the pre-existing, previously-relation-less search:analyzers id (Capella-origin) rather than to this batch's search:custom-analyzer, since the statement is about analyzers in general, not specifically custom ones; search:custom-analyzer is now recorded as isSubtypeOf search:analyzers, and both concepts' hasInternalComponent claims are consistent with each other, not competing. (2) A REAL SAME-ROUND MODELING DIVERGENCE, found by reading a concurrent sibling batch's own extraction file (server/8.0/search/default-tokenizers-reference.json) directly: that record asserts search:full-text-index -hasInternalComponent-> search:tokenizer (evidence: 'Tokenizers control how the Search Service splits input strings into individual tokens'), i.e. containment straight from the INDEX to the tokenizer, skipping the analyzer entirely. This batch (via create-custom-analyzer.json and now this page) asserts the analyzer as the intermediate container: index -> [implicitly, via configurableVia/type-mapping] -> analyzer -> tokenizer. Both are textually supportable from their own pages, but they describe two different containment DEPTHS for what is physically the same nesting (a Search index's type mapping selects an analyzer, and that analyzer is what actually contains the tokenizer) - a genuine reconciliation question, not a mistake on either side, and exactly the kind of fork this project's process is designed to surface rather than silently resolve mid-extraction. Also corroborates (a third independent statement) the set-advanced-settings.json finding that analyzer assignment is TYPE-MAPPING-scoped, not index-scoped: 'you can choose a default analyzer for your type mappings'.
